previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ , a man with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis and neurogenic bladder, was admitted with fever, cough, and shortness of breath. Initial evaluation revealed leukocytosis and urinalysis findings consistent with a urinary tract infection. Chest imaging showed no acute pulmonary process, and symptoms of respiratory infection improved during the stay. Urine culture grew Escherichia coli, sensitive to ampicillin/sulbactam, and blood cultures remained negative. He was treated with intravenous antibiotics initially, then transitioned to oral Augmentin at discharge. His baclofen pump refill was deferred, but oral baclofen was provided for muscle spasms. He received education on improved catheterization hygiene and frequency to reduce future infection risk. He was discharged home with services and instructions to follow up with his specialists.

radiology_notes.text:
CLINICAL HISTORY:  ___ male with right-sided weakness and left
pronator drift.

COMPARISON:  MR head ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Non-contrast MDCT axial images were acquired through the head. 
Coronal and sagittal reformats were obtained for evaluation.  The study was
repeated due to patient motion.

FINDINGS: There is no acute intracranial hemorrhage, edema, mass effect or
major vascular territorial infarct.  Hypodensities adjacent to the frontal
horn of the left lateral ventricle and another hypodensity in the left centrum
semiovale (4:17) are similar to ___ and likely related to multiple sclerosis
plaques.  There is no shift from normally midline structures.  Gray-white
matter differentiation is well preserved.  The basal cisterns are patent.  No
osseous abnormality is identified.  The visualized paranasal sinuses and
mastoid air cells are clear.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No acute intracranial abnormality.
2.  Hypodensities in the left frontal region are likely related to MS plaques
as seen on MRI ___.  Although there is no clear evidence for change,
repeat MR would provide a more detailed comparison and better evaluation for
white matter disease if needed clinically.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  ___ male with right-sided weakness and left
pronator drift.  Evaluate for infection.

___.

FINDINGS:  Frontal and lateral views of the chest were obtained.  The lungs
are well expanded and clear without focal consolidation, pleural effusion or
pneumothorax.  Heart size is normal.  Mediastinal silhouette and hilar
contours are normal.  A 6-mm nodule in the right lower lung is unchanged since
___, compatible with a calcified granuloma.  Cervical spinal hardware is
incompletely evaluated on this study.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intrathoracic process.
